# Day 4: Exploratory Data Analysis

**Project:** AI Operations Intelligence Platform
**Week:** 1 (Data Engineering + ML Foundation)
**Branch:** `feature/day-04-eda`
**Audience:** an AI coding agent (Antigravity) working inside the repository, supervised by the project owner.
**Prerequisite:** Days 1 to 3 are merged into `develop` and `data/processed/` has been generated by `python scripts/run_pipeline.py`.
**Deliverable:** an EDA notebook set (6 notebooks), 10 curated figures in `docs/figures/`, and a documented findings file (`docs/eda_findings.md`) that tells Days 5, 6 and 8 what the data supports, what it does not, and which modeling decisions follow.

## 0. How the Agent Must Work

1. **Read first.** Read this file completely. Then read `docs/data_pipeline.md`, `docs/data_quality_report.md`, `docs/feature_catalog.md`, `docs/data_mapping.md`, `docs/data_dictionary.md`, `docs/day02_walkthrough.md`, `docs/day03_walkthrough.md` and `data/raw/unified/timeline_metadata.json`. Section 5 of this file contains data-lineage caveats that change how findings must be written. Do not skip it.
2. **Plan before coding.** Produce a short plan (use a plan / task-list artifact if your environment supports one) listing tasks T1 to T13, the notebooks, the figures and any questions. Pause for human input only on a blocking issue (section 3).
3. **Execute tasks in order.** After each task run its acceptance checks and commit (section 14).
4. **Answer questions with numbers.** Sections 7 and 8 list numbered EDA questions (EQ1 to EQ47). Every one must be answered in the notebooks and summarized in `docs/eda_findings.md` with a number, a figure or a table. "Looks higher" is not an answer.
5. **Tag every finding with its provenance** (section 5). A finding about a synthetic effect is a *consistency check of the data generator*, not a discovery. Never present it as an insight about real operations.
6. **Do not change data or models today.** EDA reads, measures and reports. If you find a data bug, record it (section 11 and `docs/known_issues.md`). Fix it only if the fix is small, in the Day 3 pipeline code, covered by a test, and committed separately (rule R9).
7. **Finish with a walkthrough report** (`docs/day04_walkthrough.md`): files created, notebooks executed, figures produced, answers status per EQ, deviations from this spec with reasons, open questions.

## 1. Context and Objective

### Why EDA matters here

The plan lists the analysis topics: production trends, machine health, temperature, vibration, downtime, energy consumption and maintenance frequency. Day 4 covers those and adds three things this project specifically needs:

1. **Honest provenance.** Most of the data is synthetic or derived (Day 2). EDA must separate what is genuinely learned from real data (MetroPT-3 signals, Online Retail, AI4I as a dataset) from what merely reflects how the generator was written.
2. **Decisions for later days.** Day 5 needs candidate features, a normal-period definition, a time split, status thresholds and an expected anomaly base rate. Day 6 needs to know how learnable AI4I really is. Day 8 needs seasonality facts and baseline forecast scores to beat.
3. **Leakage discipline.** Statistics that drive modeling choices must come from the exploration period only (section 4, D44), and labels are used for interpretation only (D45).

### Inputs (all read-only, in `data/processed/` unless stated)

|---|---|

| `sensors.parquet` | 5-minute cleaned sensors with flags |

## 2. Non-Negotiable Rules

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| R1 | **Read-only data.** Never write into `data/raw/` or modify any file in `data/processed/` (except creating `ai4i_split_index.csv`). |
| R2 | **No models.** No training, tuning, scaling, encoding or feature selection by outcome. One exception: a shallow decision tree as a *diagnostic* in EQ45, on the AI4I training partition only, never saved, never reported as a result. |
| R3 | **Exploration period only for decisions.** Any statistic, threshold or ranking that will influence Day 5, 6 or 8 uses data inside the exploration period (D44). The holdout period may be plotted for context and used as a confirmation check, and must be labeled as such. |
| R4 | **Labels are for interpretation.** `anomaly_eval_labels.parquet` may shade charts and define event-study windows. It must not be used to choose features, thresholds or hyperparameters. |
| R5 | **Provenance tags on every finding** (section 5): `[REAL]`, `[REAL-DERIVED]`, `[SYNTHETIC-BY-DESIGN]`, `[MIXED]`. |
| R6 | **Statistics with uncertainty.** Report effect sizes with bootstrap confidence intervals (block bootstrap for time series). No p-value hunting. No claims from a single machine or a single event without saying so. |
| R7 | **Reproducible notebooks.** Seed 42, parameters in the first cell, no hidden state, run top to bottom without errors. Notebook outputs are stripped before commit (D43). |
| R8 | **Memory discipline.** Load only needed columns (`pyarrow` column selection). Do not plot raw 5-minute points for 12 machines. Aggregate to hourly or daily, or use hexbin/ECDF. |
| R9 | **Pipeline fixes are exceptional.** If EDA reveals a bug, log it in `docs/known_issues.md` first. A fix is allowed only if small, in Day 3 pipeline code, with a unit test, in its own commit `fix(data): ...`, followed by a pipeline re-run and an update of the affected notebooks. Larger problems are logged, not fixed. |
| R10 | **No Day 5+ work.** No anomaly scoring, no failure model, no forecasting model. Naive baselines for benchmarks (EQ38) are the only "forecasts" allowed. |
| R11 | **Plot quality.** Every figure has a title, axis labels with units, a legend where needed, readable fonts, a colorblind-safe palette, and a one-line caption in `docs/eda_findings.md`. |
| R12 | **Code quality.** Reusable logic lives in `ml/eda/`, not copied between notebooks. `ruff check .` passes on `ml/eda/` and tests. |

## 3. Human Prerequisites and Stop Conditions

### Prerequisites

- Day 3 merged. `data/processed/` populated (the agent verifies in T1).
- Python dev dependencies installed (`pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`). Day 4 adds `statsmodels` and `nbstripout` (T1).
- No database is needed. EDA reads Parquet files.

### Stop and ask the human when

- Any file listed under Inputs is missing and cannot be regenerated by `python scripts/run_pipeline.py`.
- Fewer than **2 real failure windows** fall inside the exploration period (D44). Report the counts and options: (a) raise the exploration fraction to 0.8 and document it, (b) keep 0.7 and use all real windows in the event study as **descriptive-only** with that label. The human decides.
- The `timeline_metadata.json` does not say which signals the Day 2 failure-window overlay modified (section 5, caveat C3). Do not guess.
- The planted-effects recovery check (EQ4) shows a mismatch larger than the tolerances in T4. That suggests a pipeline or generator bug.

### Do NOT stop for

- Differences between approximate numbers quoted in this file and the actual data. Record the actual numbers.
- Missing optional pieces (the stretch EQ30 raw MetroPT check).

## 4. Decisions for Day 4

Record these in `docs/architecture.md` under "Decision Log" (continue after D41 from Day 3).

| # | Decision | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| D42 | Notebook layout | **6 notebooks** (overview, production, sensors, maintenance and failures, retail, AI4I) with shared helpers in `ml/eda/` | One giant notebook becomes unreadable and unmaintainable |
| D43 | Notebook storage | Commit notebooks **with outputs stripped** (`nbstripout`). Commit the curated figures in `docs/figures/` | Keeps Git diffs small. Figures are the reviewable artifact |
| D44 | Time split for EDA | **Exploration period = first 70 percent of the sensor window by date. Holdout = last 30 percent.** Fraction in `ml/eda/config.py` (`EXPLORATION_FRACTION = 0.7`) | Protects the data later used for model evaluation from influencing modeling decisions |
| D45 | Label usage | Labels are for interpretation only (R4) | Prevents label leakage through human choices |
| D46 | AI4I split | **Stratified 80/20 train/test split** on `Machine failure`, seed 42, saved as an index file. EDA uses the **training partition only** | Protects the AI4I test set. Day 6 reuses the same index |
| D47 | Finding provenance | Every finding carries a provenance tag (section 5) | The data is mostly synthetic. Readers must know what a finding is worth |
| D48 | Statistical reporting | Effect sizes with bootstrap CIs, block bootstrap (block length 7 days for daily, 24 hours for hourly) for time series. No significance testing across many comparisons | Time series are autocorrelated. Many comparisons inflate false positives |
| D49 | Data access | EDA reads Parquet, not PostgreSQL | Faster, no infrastructure dependency |
| D50 | Baseline benchmarks | Naive baselines for forecasting are computed by **rolling-origin evaluation on a validation slice inside the exploration period** (the last 28 days of the exploration period) | Gives Day 8 realistic numbers to beat without touching the holdout |
| D51 | Plot standards | Matplotlib/Seaborn with one shared style (`ml/eda/plotting.py`), colorblind-safe palette, 150 dpi, width 10 inches, PNG | Consistent portfolio-quality figures |
| D52 | Data changes | None on Day 4 except documented exceptional fixes (R9) | EDA must not silently alter what it analyzes |

## 5. Data Provenance and Caveats (read carefully)

### Provenance tags

| Tag | Meaning | How to write the finding |
|---|---|---|
| `[REAL]` | Comes from real measurements or real transactions (MetroPT-3 pressure, motor current, COMP state; Online Retail; AI4I rows as a dataset) | May be stated as an observation. Still time-shifted and still a limited sample |
| `[REAL-DERIVED]` | Deterministic transformation of real values (for example energy computed from real motor current) | State the transformation |
| `[SYNTHETIC-BY-DESIGN]` | Produced by a Day 2 generator (vibration, RPM, production, downtime, maintenance, scenario episodes, derived machines' behavior) | Describe as "consistent with the generator design" or "recovers the planted effect". Never as a real-world discovery |
| `[MIXED]` | Mixes real and synthetic parts | State which part drives the finding |

### Known caveats the agent must apply

| # | Caveat | Consequence for EDA |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | **Vibration, RPM, production, downtime, maintenance and scenario episodes are synthetic.** | Relationships among them (for example vibration versus motor current) hold **by construction**. High correlations there are not evidence of physics. Tag `[SYNTHETIC-BY-DESIGN]` |
| C2 | **Only M-104 uses the real MetroPT signal series.** The 11 other machines are built by resampling the same pool of healthy MetroPT days with scale factors (Day 2 decision D17). | Machines are **not independent**. Cross-machine similarity is partly an artifact. Report the pairwise correlation (EQ5) and do not treat 12 machines as 12 independent samples |
| C3 | **The Day 2 failure-window overlay modified synthetic and some real-signal columns for M-104.** Day 2 task 4a applied a vibration multiplier and a temperature offset before and inside each real failure window, plus an RPM reduction inside it. | In the real windows, `vibration`, `rpm` and `temperature` are **overlay-affected**. Only `pressure`, `motor_current` and `comp_state` are unmodified real signals (energy is derived from current, so it is unaffected unless current was changed). The M-104 event study (EQ26) must therefore be split into **real-only signals** and **overlay-affected signals**. Verify the exact list in `timeline_metadata.json` (stop condition) |
| C4 | **M-104 final 35 days contain synthetic hero degradation.** | It lies in the holdout period by construction. It is a demo storyline, not evidence. Tag `[SYNTHETIC-BY-DESIGN]` |
| C5 | **Time shifted data.** MetroPT and Online Retail were shifted by whole weeks. | Absolute dates are not real. Weekday and time-of-day patterns are preserved. Do not interpret calendar dates as historical facts |
| C6 | **AI4I is synthetic and rule-generated, with no time or machine dimension.** | Findings describe the dataset, not real machines. Metrics later may be unrealistically high (Day 6). EQ45 quantifies this |
| C7 | **Retail data is retail, not manufacturing demand.** | Demand patterns are used as a demand signal for the demo. Do not claim anything about manufacturing |
| C8 | **Gaps in M-104** are real and left unfilled beyond 15 minutes (Day 3). | Report coverage. Do not fill gaps in EDA |

### Planted-effects recovery check (EQ4)

Because the data generator is known, EDA can **verify the pipeline by recovering the planted effects**. This is a quality check, not a finding. Expected values come from Day 2 (`docs/data_mapping.md`, `docs/day02_walkthrough.md`); the tolerance column is the maximum acceptable gap before the agent must log a possible bug.

| Planted effect (source) | Measure in EDA | Tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| Weekend production factor 0.6 | Weekend production divided by weekday production per machine | within 0.08 |
| Healthy machines: vibration below 4.5 mm/s | Share of exploration-period readings below 4.5 for machines with scenario `healthy` | at least 99.5 percent |
| M-103 drift: weekly mean vibration about 5.0 in the final 7 days | Final 7 days mean | between 4.5 and 5.8 |
| M-104 hero degradation: last 24 hours mean vibration at least 7.0 | Final 24 hours mean | at least 7.0 |
| Inspection about every 500 operating hours | Median operating hours between inspections per machine | within 15 percent of 500 |
| Preventive about every 2,000 operating hours | Median operating hours between preventive events | within 15 percent of 2,000 |
| Orders follow retail demand index | Correlation between `orders` (fleet daily sum) and retail daily sales/revenue index | at least 0.5 |
| `business_daily` equals `production` | Row-level equality | exact |

## 6. Shared Setup

### 6.1 Package layout

```text
ml/eda/
├── __init__.py
├── config.py        # constants (exploration fraction, seeds, thresholds, palette)
├── load.py          # cached loaders with column selection
├── splits.py        # exploration / holdout masks, AI4I stratified split
├── plotting.py      # shared style, save_fig, shading helpers
└── stats.py         # bootstrap CI, block bootstrap, effect sizes, ECDF, event study, robust z, ACF helper
```

### 6.2 `ml/eda/config.py`

```python
from pathlib import Path
from ml.preprocessing.config import ROOT, PROCESSED, SEED, VIB_WARNING, VIB_CRITICAL, TEMP_MAX_SPEC

EXPLORATION_FRACTION = 0.7
VALIDATION_DAYS = 28            # validation slice for baseline forecasts (D50)
AI4I_TEST_FRACTION = 0.2
BOOTSTRAP_ITERATIONS = 2000
FIGURES = ROOT / "docs" / "figures"
NOTEBOOKS = ROOT / "ml" / "notebooks"
AI4I_CSV = ROOT / "data" / "raw" / "ai4i"           # resolve the file by pattern, as Day 2 did
AI4I_SPLIT_INDEX = PROCESSED / "ai4i_split_index.csv"
# Colorblind-safe categorical palette (Okabe-Ito)
PALETTE = ["#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#009E73", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#56B4E9", "#F0E442", "#000000"]
```

### 6.3 Helper requirements

**`load.py`**
- `load_ops(columns=None)`, `load_sensors(columns=None, machines=None)`, `load_sensor_features(columns)`, `load_maintenance()`, `load_machines()`, `load_labels()`, `load_transactions()`, `load_business_daily()`, `load_product_demand()`, `load_ai4i()` (raw CSV, with columns renamed to snake_case without units: `udi, product_id, type, air_temp_k, process_temp_k, rpm, torque_nm, tool_wear_min, machine_failure, twf, hdf, pwf, osf, rnf`).
- Column selection through `pyarrow`. Timestamps in UTC. `lru_cache` where safe.

**`splits.py`**
- `exploration_cutoff()` returns the first timestamp of the holdout: the date at the `EXPLORATION_FRACTION` quantile of the sensor window dates (whole days, 00:00 UTC).
- `is_exploration(ts)` and `is_holdout(ts)` masks for timestamps and dates. They are disjoint, chronological, and cover the whole window.
- `make_ai4i_split()` returns a DataFrame (`udi`, `partition` with `train` or `test`) using `sklearn.model_selection.train_test_split(stratify=machine_failure, random_state=SEED)`. `save_ai4i_split()` writes it to `AI4I_SPLIT_INDEX`. `load_ai4i(partition="train")` filters by that index.

**`plotting.py`**
- `apply_style()` sets rcParams (font sizes, grid, palette, figure width 10 inches, dpi 150).
- `save_fig(fig, name)` writes to `docs/figures/{name}.png`, creates the folder, uses `bbox_inches="tight"`, never overwrites silently outside its own name, returns the path.
- `shade_episodes(ax, labels_df, machine_id, ...)` shades label intervals with distinct colors for real versus synthetic episodes and adds legend entries.
- `add_thresholds(ax, kind)` draws the manual thresholds (vibration 4.5 and 7.0, temperature 85).
- `mark_holdout(ax)` draws a vertical line at the exploration cutoff with the text "holdout".

**`stats.py`**
- `bootstrap_ci(values, stat=np.mean, n=BOOTSTRAP_ITERATIONS, alpha=0.05, seed=SEED)`
- `block_bootstrap_ci(series, block_len, stat, n, alpha, seed)` for autocorrelated data (moving-block bootstrap)
- `cohens_d(a, b)`, `ratio_with_ci(a, b, ...)` (ratio of means with bootstrap interval)
- `ecdf(values)` returns sorted values and cumulative probabilities
- `robust_z(series, window, ...)` trailing median and MAD z-score (same definition as Day 3 Tier 2, reuse that function if importable)
- `event_study(df, event_times, signal, pre_hours, post_hours, baseline_window)` returns a hourly DataFrame (hours relative to event start, one column per event, plus median and range), baseline-normalized
- `acf_values(series, nlags)` (thin wrapper around `statsmodels.tsa.stattools.acf`)

## 7. Tasks

### T1: Branch, environment and verification (about 20 min)

1. `git checkout develop && git pull && git checkout -b feature/day-04-eda`
2. Activate venv. Add `statsmodels>=0.14` and `nbstripout>=0.7` to `requirements-dev.txt`. `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Run `nbstripout --install` so notebook outputs are stripped by a Git filter.
3. Verify every input file exists (section 1). If `data/processed/` is empty, run `python scripts/run_pipeline.py --skip-db` (full run). Stop if it fails.
4. Read `docs/data_quality_report.md` and list in the draft walkthrough: known gaps (M-104), flagged shares, any warnings.
5. Create `ml/eda/` with the files in section 6.1 (empty modules for now), `ml/notebooks/` folder entries, and `docs/figures/.gitkeep` if missing.
6. Inspect `timeline_metadata.json` and record in the draft walkthrough: shift values, overlay flags per signal for the failure windows, episode definitions (caveat C3 stop condition).

**Acceptance:** all inputs found; `nbstripout --status` shows it installed; metadata summary written.

---

### T2: Helper modules and tests (about 60 min)

Implement section 6.3 fully and create `tests/test_eda.py`.

| Test | Assertion |
|---|---|
| Split masks | exploration and holdout are disjoint, chronological (every exploration timestamp earlier than every holdout timestamp), and together cover all timestamps |
| Cutoff | cutoff falls at 00:00 UTC, fraction of days in exploration within one day of 0.7 |
| AI4I split | stratified (failure share within 0.5 percentage points between partitions), disjoint, deterministic (same output twice), sizes 80/20 |
| Bootstrap CI | deterministic with fixed seed, CI contains the true mean for a known normal sample |
| Block bootstrap | wider interval than the plain bootstrap for a strongly autocorrelated synthetic series |
| ECDF | monotonic, ends at 1.0 |
| Event study | on a crafted series with a known step at the event, the aligned median shows the step at hour 0, baseline-normalized values are around 1 before the event |
| Robust z | spike in an otherwise flat series gives a large z, no leakage from the future (changing later values does not change earlier z) |
| `save_fig` | writes the PNG, returns the path, file is non-empty |

**Acceptance:** `pytest tests/test_eda.py -v` passes. `ruff check ml/eda tests/test_eda.py` passes.

---

### T3: AI4I split index (about 15 min)

**Acceptance:** `data/processed/ai4i_split_index.csv` exists (git-ignored) and the test partition is never loaded by any notebook (grep the notebooks for `partition="test"` or `"test"` filters in T12).

### T4: Notebook 01, Overview, lineage and planted-effects recovery (about 40 min)

**File:** `ml/notebooks/01_overview_and_lineage.ipynb`

Cell 1 holds parameters (`EXPLORATION_FRACTION`, seed). Required content:

| EQ | Question | Output |
|---|---|---|
| EQ1 | What is the coverage of the data? | Table: per machine, first/last timestamp, number of days, share of valid intervals (`sensor_coverage`), complete days count. Exploration versus holdout date ranges and row counts |
| EQ2 | How much of the data was imputed, flagged or missing? | Table per machine: imputed share, gap rows, longest gap, Tier 1 faults, Tier 2 flag rate. M-104 gaps listed with start, end, duration |
| EQ3 | What is the lineage of each column? | Table (signal, provenance tag, source, transformation) from `docs/data_mapping.md`. State caveats C1 to C8 explicitly |
| EQ4 | Do the planted effects recover? | The recovery table from section 5, with measured value, expected value, tolerance and PASS/FAIL |
| EQ5 | How independent are the machines? | Pairwise correlation matrix of **daily mean vibration** and **daily mean temperature** among derived machines in the exploration period (healthy episodes only). Median off-diagonal correlation. State the independence caveat (C2) with the number |

**Acceptance:** notebook runs top to bottom. Every EQ has a numeric answer. Any FAIL in EQ4 is logged in `docs/known_issues.md` with a diagnosis attempt.

**File:** `ml/notebooks/02_production_downtime_energy.ipynb`. Data: `operations_dataset.parquet`.

|---|---|---|

| EQ23 | Who is overdue and since when? | Daily `inspection_overdue` and `preventive_overdue` shares per machine over time. Expect M-104 and M-107 to become overdue |
| EQ24 | What is the failure history? | Corrective events per machine, time between failures, failure types (all failure types come from Day 2 sampling, so tag `[SYNTHETIC-BY-DESIGN]`; M-104 events are real windows with synthetic labels `Air Leak`) |
| EQ25 | Does time since maintenance relate to signal level? | Vibration and temperature (daily mean) versus `days_since_preventive` and `operating_hours_since_preventive`, healthy-ish machines, exploration period. Describe the shape and say plainly that any relationship is planted or absent |
| EQ26 | **What happens to M-104's signals before and during real failures?** | **Event study** aligned to each real window start (hours −72 to +24, plus the baseline window −14 to −3 days), baseline-normalized. Present **two panels**: (a) real-only signals (`pressure`, `motor_current`, `comp_state` running ratio) and (b) overlay-affected signals (`vibration`, `temperature`, `rpm`) tagged `[SYNTHETIC-BY-DESIGN]` (caveat C3). One thin line per window, median and range |
| EQ27 | How much lead time does each signal give? | For each signal and window: first hour at which the robust z-score stays above 3 for 6 consecutive hours (trailing baseline of 14 days). Table of lead time hours, with "none" where it never triggers. Real-only signals reported separately. Windows in the holdout period are flagged as confirmation-only (R3) |
| EQ28 | What do synthetic failure precursors look like on other machines? | Same event study for M-105, M-110, M-111 (events defined by the metadata). Tag `[SYNTHETIC-BY-DESIGN]`. Compare shapes with the M-104 overlay (they should look alike, because they use the same overlay) |
| EQ29 | What does maintenance do to signals? | Before/after comparison around the M-106 preventive event (10 days either side) on daily vibration and temperature. Tag `[SYNTHETIC-BY-DESIGN]` |
| EQ30 | **Stretch.** Do the native MetroPT channels carry a real precursor? | Read the raw MetroPT CSV read-only (apply the time shift from the metadata), hourly means for `TP2`, `TP3`, `H1`, `DV_pressure`, `Reservoirs`, `Oil_temperature`, `Motor_current`. Same event study around the real windows. Compare against the baseline period. Conclusion for Day 5: whether adding native channels for M-104 would improve evaluation honesty. Skip if time is short and say so |

Figures produced here: **F07** (M-104 event study, both panels) and **F08** (maintenance frequency, cost and interval compliance).

**Important for the write-up:** because of caveat C3, the lead time found in the vibration and temperature panels is **designed** into the data. The scientifically meaningful result is whether the **real-only** signals move before the failure. State that conclusion clearly, whichever way it goes.

**Acceptance:** all EQ answered (EQ30 optional). F07 and F08 saved. The distinction between real-only and overlay-affected signals is explicit in both the figure and the findings.

## 9. Statistical Reporting Guide (for the agent)

- **Means and ratios:** report with 95 percent bootstrap CI. For daily or hourly series use the moving-block bootstrap (D48).
- **Group comparisons:** report effect size (Cohen's d or ratio of means) with CI. Do not run dozens of pairwise tests.
- **Correlations:** use Spearman. State sample size, and note autocorrelation reduces the effective sample size.
- **Proportions:** Wilson interval or bootstrap.
- **Multiple comparisons:** if more than 10 comparisons feed one conclusion, say so and downgrade the confidence level.
- **Small samples:** the number of real failure windows is small (record the count). Any statement based on them has `low` confidence regardless of how clean the picture looks.
- **Time series assumptions:** do not treat consecutive intervals as independent. Do not compute p-values on raw 5-minute data.
- **Report negatives:** "no precursor visible in real-only signals" is a valid, valuable finding.

## 11. Challenges, Risks and Mitigations

| # | Challenge | Why it matters | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Presenting synthetic effects as discoveries** | Misleads readers and recruiters, undermines the project's credibility | Provenance tags (D47), planted-effects recovery table, wording rules in T11 |
| 2 | **Overlay on M-104 failure windows** (C3) | Vibration and temperature precursors exist by design, so Day 5 evaluation on those signals would be circular | Split event study into real-only and overlay-affected (EQ26, EQ27). Stretch EQ30. Explicit Day 5 handoff recommendation |
| 3 | **Non-independent machines** (C2) | Cross-machine statistics look more convincing than they are | EQ5 correlation, effective-sample caveat, avoid fleet-level significance claims |
| 4 | **Peeking at the holdout** | Biases thresholds and feature choices that Day 5 evaluates later | D44, R3, helpers that mark the holdout, confirmation-only labeling |
| 5 | **Label usage** | Choosing features because they separate labeled windows is leakage | D45, R4, grep check in T12 |
| 6 | **Few real failure events** | Any conclusion has wide uncertainty | Count reported, confidence level `low`, descriptive wording, no generalization |
| 7 | **Autocorrelated data and many comparisons** | False confidence from naive tests | D48, section 9 guide, block bootstrap |
| 8 | **Overplotting and memory** | About 0.8 million 5-minute rows | Hourly or daily aggregation, ECDF, column selection (R8) |
| 9 | **AI4I test contamination** | Day 6 evaluation becomes optimistic | D46, training partition only, grep check |
| 10 | **AI4I looks trivially learnable** | Day 6 metrics could be inflated | EQ44 to EQ47 quantify rule-likeness and define honest reporting |
| 11 | **Retail anomalies** (large order and cancellation pairs, non-product codes, guests) | Distorts KPIs and seasonality | Day 3 flags, KPI-eligible rows only, state exclusions in figures |
| 12 | **Notebook sprawl and hidden state** | Unreproducible results | 6 focused notebooks, helpers in `ml/eda/`, parameters cell, `make eda-run` |
| 13 | **Notebook outputs bloating Git** | Large diffs and repo size | `nbstripout`, committed figures only |
| 14 | **Time-boxing** | EDA expands without limit | Fixed question list, time plan (section 15), stretch items clearly marked |
| 15 | **Narrative without numbers** | Findings that cannot be checked | Rule: each EQ has a number, table or figure. Findings table requires evidence column |
| 16 | **Bugs discovered late** | Pipeline errors propagate into models | EQ4 recovery checks, `known_issues.md`, R9 for small fixes |
| 17 | **Mixed time handling** | Off-by-one-day errors in daily versus 5-minute data | UTC everywhere, use the helper masks, tests |

## 12. Handoff to Day 5 (add to `docs/architecture.md` "Next Steps")

Write these in the findings document as the **decision register** and copy the headline items into the architecture doc.

**For Day 5 (anomaly detection, Isolation Forest):**
1. **Candidate feature shortlist** with rationale from EQ13 to EQ18 (for example current, temperature, pressure, RPM, energy, vibration, plus selected rolling features). Per-machine baselines are computed on Day 5 (D39).
2. **Normal-period definition and time split:** use the exploration period for fitting, the holdout for evaluation. State which machines and episodes are excluded from the "normal" training set (scenario episodes and failure windows must not be in it).
3. **Evaluation honesty:** because of caveat C3, evaluate on M-104 twice: (a) all features and (b) **real-only features** (`pressure`, `motor_current`, `comp_state` and any native channels recommended by EQ30). Report both. Do not present (a) alone as detection performance.
4. **Threshold proposals** for `anomaly_status` from the exploration period (table in the findings).
5. **Expected anomaly base rates and contamination range** (EQ19).
6. **False-positive stress test:** M-109 (benign spikes) must not be flagged as critical.

**For Day 6 (failure prediction):**
1. Use `data/processed/ai4i_split_index.csv`. Training partition for fitting and cross-validation, test partition for the final evaluation only.
2. Exclude `twf`, `hdf`, `pwf`, `osf`, `rnf`, `udi`, `product_id` from features (EQ46).
3. Use the engineered features from EQ44. Report PR-AUC, recall at fixed precision, calibration and confusion matrix, with the prevalence baseline (EQ40, EQ47).
4. State in the README that AI4I labels are rule-generated and metrics overstate real-world performance (EQ45).
5. Open question OQ-1 (how demo machines feed the model) still needs a decision.

**For Day 8 (forecasting):**
1. Seasonality: weekly (period 7) per EQ7, EQ31, EQ37.
2. Baselines to beat: the EQ38 benchmark table.
3. Evaluation protocol: rolling origin, 7-day horizon, validation inside the exploration period, final check on the holdout.

## 13. What NOT to Do on Day 4

- Do not train, tune, score or evaluate any model (the EQ45 diagnostic tree is the only exception, and it is never reported as a result).
- Do not select features or thresholds by looking at labeled windows or at the holdout.
- Do not examine the AI4I test partition.
- Do not scale, encode, impute or otherwise transform data for modeling.
- Do not modify `data/processed/` files or the raw data.
- Do not present synthetic-by-design effects as discoveries.
- Do not claim physical relationships for derived signals (vibration, RPM).
- Do not build API endpoints, database changes or frontend pages.
- Do not generate RAG documents.
- Do not commit notebook outputs or data files.

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python scripts/check_env.py
ls data/processed                      # inputs present
```

### Merge and tag

```bash
git push -u origin feature/day-04-eda
gh pr create --base develop --head feature/day-04-eda \
  --title "Day 4: Exploratory data analysis and findings" \
  --body "See docs/day04_walkthrough.md and docs/eda_findings.md"
# after review and merge:
git checkout develop && git pull
git tag -a day-04-complete -m "Day 4: EDA complete"
git push origin day-04-complete
git checkout -b feature/day-05-anomaly-detection
```

Before merging, review the PR for: no data files, no notebook outputs, no secrets, no absolute paths, and that every figure in the diff has a caption in `docs/eda_findings.md`.
